topics.label: Lecture Introduction and Learning Outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer opens the session by linking histopathology practicals to the lecture objectives on cancer genetics.

topics.label: Discovery of Oncogenes Through Tumor Virology
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics trace how the study of infectious disease and tumor virology revealed that oncogenes originate from normal cellular genes.

topics.label: Experimental Assays for Cellular Transformation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the laboratory assays used to demonstrate cell transformation and measure the functional impact of cancer-associated mutations.

topics.label: Classification and Mechanisms of Oncogenes and Tumor Suppressors
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how oncogenes and tumor suppressor genes differ in their mutational effects and regulatory roles in cell cycle checkpoints.

topics.label: Mechanisms and Consequences of Genetic Instability
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the origins, mechanisms, and cellular consequences of chromosomal and sequence instability in cancer cells.

topics.label: Multi-Step Tumorigenesis and Mutation Progression
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explores the multi-step model of cancer progression driven by the sequential acquisition of genetic alterations.

topics.label: Hereditary Cancer Predisposition Syndromes
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics address how inherited mutations accelerate cancer development across specific hereditary predisposition syndromes.
